anndata.claude

Source: CONTEXT.md

An R port of Python anndata (reference release 0.13.4) for annotated data matrices and their on-disk formats.

Language

The object

AnnData: An annotated data matrix of n_obs observations by n_vars variables, with aligned annotations and unstructured metadata. Avoid: SingleCellExperiment, Seurat object, dataset

Observation: A row of an AnnData, usually a cell. Avoid: sample, column

Variable: A column of an AnnData, usually a gene or feature. Avoid: feature, row

Slot: One named component of an AnnData: X, obs, var, obsm, varm, obsp, varp, layers, uns or raw. Avoid: field, attribute, assay

obs_names / var_names: The string identifiers of observations and variables, which may contain duplicates. Avoid: rownames, colnames, barcodes

Aligned mapping: A slot holding named elements whose dimensions must match n_obs and/or n_vars (obsm, varm, obsp, varp, layers).

uns: The slot holding unstructured metadata as a nested mapping of arbitrary encodable values.

View: An AnnData produced by subsetting that shares data with its parent until modified, when it becomes an independent copy. Avoid: slice, subset object

raw: A frozen copy of X, var and varm kept from before variable filtering, sharing observations with its parent.

On disk

Element: A single stored value in a file (array, sparse matrix, dataframe, mapping or scalar) identified by its path.

Encoding type: The encoding-type attribute naming how an Element is stored, such as csr_matrix, dataframe or categorical.

Encoding version: The encoding-version attribute giving the version of an Encoding type’s layout.

On-disk dtype: The exact storage type of an Element’s data (e.g. float32, int64, uint8), which R may not represent natively.

Round trip: Reading a file and writing it back (R to R, Python to R to Python or R to Python to R) so that every Element keeps its Encoding type, Encoding version, On-disk dtype and values, and the object read is equal whichever language read or wrote it. Avoid: conversion, export

Structural equivalence: Two Stores (of the same or different formats) with the same tree of groups and arrays, attributes, Encoding types and versions, On-disk dtypes, shapes and values, regardless of byte layout. Avoid: identical files

Store: A file or directory holding an AnnData on disk: an h5ad file or a zarr store (v2 or v3). Avoid: container

Shard: A zarr v3 file holding many chunks of one array with an index, written by default by Python (auto_shard_zarr_v3). Shard and chunk layout are not part of Structural equivalence.

Consolidated metadata: All of a zarr store’s group and array metadata collected in one place (.zmetadata in v2, the root zarr.json in v3) so it can be read at once.

Reference implementation: Python anndata at the pinned release, the only source of truth for behaviour.
